content.title: Overwhelmed by Parenting? Reflect on Your Own Childhood First
content.subtitle: If they had walked away back then, where would we be today?
content.body:
When the Pressures of a Busy Life Leave Us Impatient

By the end of the day, we are exhausted. From morning till night, we juggle office work, traffic jams, career pressures, family struggles, and responsibilities toward our in-laws. Life feels like an endless battle, leaving us with barely any time to catch our breath. Yet, when our little child becomes a bit too mischievous, makes demands, screams for no apparent reason, or creates a mess, we lose our patience in an instant. We snap at them in frustration, feel overwhelmed, or perhaps even raise a hand in anger. Deep inside, we sigh, “I just can’t take it anymore!” But in these moments of exhaustion, do we ever stop to ask ourselves: What were we like as children?

Our Parents Protected Us While Carrying the Burden of a Large Household

Let us close our eyes and look back at the days we have left behind. There was a time when most families lived in extended households. Meals for 10, 15, or even 20 people were prepared at home every day. From early dawn until midnight, our mothers managed the entire household, accommodating everyone’s different preferences, temperaments, and needs. Despite the exhausting workload, they never turned away from raising us out of sheer fatigue. Meanwhile, our fathers worked day and night tirelessly to support the family, fund our education, and secure our future.

We, too, were once innocent children. We played mischievously, kept our parents awake night after night, and tested their patience. Even while carrying the burden of a large household and enduring financial hardship and physical exhaustion, did our parents turn away from us in frustration?

Where Would We Be Today If They Had Turned Away?

If our parents had given up on us because of our disobedience or mischief, would we have grown into the people we are today, standing tall in society? When managing just one or two children tests our patience, do we remember the mother who lovingly fed us with a smile even when she was unwell? Do we remember the father who wore torn shoes to pay our school fees?

If our parents have passed away, do we raise our hands in every prayer, asking our Lord to forgive them? And if they are still alive, do we make time in our busy lives to check on them? Do we look at them with affection and sit down for a heartfelt conversation? Or have we neglected them under the excuse of career demands and modern life?

Repaying Their Sacrifices

No worldly wealth can ever repay our parents’ selfless sacrifices. What we can do is pray for their mercy with every breath: “My Lord, have mercy on them as they raised me with love when I was little.” We can also continue good deeds with the intention of seeking their forgiveness and spiritual peace, so that their reward continues to reach them.

There is another timeless truth we must remember: time never stands still. Life moves forward at its own pace. If we forget our parents’ sacrifices today, using our busy lives as an excuse to neglect our responsibilities, will our children remember us when we grow old and frail? Our children are quietly learning from how we treat our parents today. If we show them neglect, can we expect them to treat us differently tomorrow?
